basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment is common in pathogenic 9q duplications; skeletal and cardiac abnormalities vary substantially by duplicated segment.
Neurodevelopmental impairment predominates among pathogenic chromosome 21 imbalances; other organ damage is not consistent across this heterogeneous umbrella.
Defined as an acquired metabolic disorder; no additional organ damage is shared across its diverse subtypes.
A mass-forming tuberculous infection; the anatomical site is unspecified and may vary.
Squamous carcinoma arising predominantly in the anal canal; perianal skin origin is a subset. HPV association does not make the carcinoma an infection.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; cerebral/cerebellar atrophy, seizures and hepatic failure occurred in 1/1 reported patient, supporting both organs with limited evidence.
Retinal degeneration defines the disease. Bronchiectasis occurred in 1/4 patients (25%); situs inversus alone does not establish organ damage.
Mesenchymal hamartoma most often denotes a hepatic lesion; this site-unspecified umbrella also includes subcutaneous lesions, making organ assignment uncertain.
Skin lesions, intraosseous odontogenic jaw cysts and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome. Falx calcification usually causes no neurologic damage.
Progressive visual loss, scoliosis and arachnodactyly are defining features; ocular and skeletal abnormalities occur in 80-99%.
Hypertrophy of the pyloric wall causes gastric outlet obstruction; dehydration and associated electrolyte changes are secondary consequences.
Cleft palate, ocular colobomata and radial synostosis define three organ axes; deafness is also a defining feature and qualifies as otologic involvement.
Otosclerosis affects the otic capsule and sound transmission; hearing impairment occurred in 7/7 patients.
An intraductal breast lesion; breast is outside the specified organ axes.
Phenylalanine metabolism disorder; untreated classic disease causes severe intellectual disability and persistent neurologic injury in most patients.
Congenital nonfunctioning lung tissue defines the disease; an anomalous systemic feeding artery does not itself establish cardiovascular damage.
Defined by hepatic steatosis with alcohol exposure and cardiometabolic risk factors; those risk factors do not establish additional organ involvement.
Developmental delay occurred in 3/3; optic nerve hypoplasia and amblyopia in 1/1 examined support direct ocular impairment, although evidence is limited.
Immune-mediated dermatomyositis with skin disease and objective subclinical myositis; interstitial lung disease affects roughly 30-50% of clinically amyopathic cases.
Developmental abnormalities of maxillofacial bones define the disorder. Speech delay and pinna morphology lack evidence of common additional functional damage.
An isolated inherited dilated cardiomyopathy; ventricular dysfunction, heart failure and mitral regurgitation occurred in 10/10 patients.
Defined as injury to cerebral blood vessels and classified as both cerebrovascular disease and brain injury.
HPV infection produces papillary lesions of perianal and external genital skin; internal anal involvement is not established as common across the concept.
Conductive deafness and stapedial ear malformation define otologic disease; associated facial palsy establishes facial nerve dysfunction.
Inherited fibrinogen coagulation defect. Bleeding alone does not establish other organ damage; the supplied cataract, cardiac and malformation annotations are discordant.
